text:
jamie: Heads-up — last night the EU backfill + long-context streaming batch hit peering limits between az-a and az-b and bumped GPU run-rate ~32%. Observed: average seq len jumped from ~1.8k -> 2.6k, streaming tokens up ~45%. Logs show TCP retransmits on peering links.

priya: ugh. any single job causing it or lots of concurrent streaming sessions?

jamie: mix — a handful of customer backfills (non-streaming) + many new interactive streaming sessions. Backfills are heavy KV-cache warmers (large prefixes) and we also had daily "catch-up" backfill cron at 01:00 that overlaps with EU peak.

omar: can we throttle the backfill window? move to 04:00? If peering saturates, tail latencies spike and we start failing SLOs.

lisa: quick numbers: projected GPU-hours for eu-west next 30d increased by ~28% if context growth holds. If streaming adoption keeps growing we hit committed capacity by mid-July.

priya: propose immediate mitigations: 1) reduce backfill concurrency (scale down job to 1 replica), 2) increase kvcache eviction so warmers are lighter, 3) rate-limit streaming fallback to non-streaming models. Thoughts?

jamie: agree. Also we should consider routing policy: prefer az-c for heavy backfills (peering path different) and drain az-b for background batch traffic during 00:00-06:00.

omar: k8s changes are simple: 
```
kubectl -n ops scale job backfill-job --replicas=1
kubectl -n ops annotate nodeSelector "backfill=az-c" --overwrite
```
But we need to coordinate with autoscaler to avoid killing burst capacity for realtime.

lisa: cost note — moving backfills shifts GPU-hours but increases inter-AZ egress slightly. Expected net cost change ~+3% if we add 3x A100s in az-c vs scheduling smarter. Adding reserved capacity (3 GPUs) would cost ~€2.1k/mo but prevent mid-July overage spikes.

priya: immediate plan: jamie to reduce backfill concurrency and push kvcache TTL change; omar to add az-c nodeSelector and hold autoscaler scaling rules; lisa to run 30d run-rate projection and cost delta; I'll monitor peering metrics and SLOs.

jamie: doing now — scaling backfill and bumping kvcache eviction from 72h -> 12h for warmers only.

k8s-bot: deploy started for backfill-job scaling (job/backfill-job) — 1 -> 1 replicas (no change in desired, rolling restart).

omar: added nodeSelector to backfill job template, requeued. Please confirm if any customer jobs hit backfill window.

lisa: putting a short-term buy option in procurement for 3x A100 in eu-west-1c pending final numbers.

priya: monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/eu-peering - alert set if 95th percentile p95 latency > 120ms or peering util > 78%.

jamie: follow-up: let's run a short experiment this weekend — disable backfill for 6 hours and replay at 04:00 to assert effect on run-rate. If that reduces GPU-hours by >20% and lowers peering util, we keep the schedule change.

omar: ack. I'll patch the cron and add a canary rollout for the schedule.

lisa: FYI I'll include a seasonal modifier in the capacity spreadsheet assuming +15% baseline growth for summer, +30% streaming adoption for new customers.

priya: perfect. thanks all. :thumbsup:
